Shred destination selection and Turbine tree sampling for staked and unstaked validators.

# Purpose
This C file implements `fd_shred_dest`, which computes shred destination indices for a validator set. It builds and manages the state needed to map validator public keys to validator indices, split the validator list into staked and unstaked groups, and use that state to select shred targets. The file also defines the memory footprint and object life cycle functions [`fd_shred_dest_footprint`](<#fd_shred_dest_footprint>), [`fd_shred_dest_new`](<#fd_shred_dest_new>), [`fd_shred_dest_join`](<#fd_shred_dest_join>), [`fd_shred_dest_leave`](<#fd_shred_dest_leave>), and [`fd_shred_dest_delete`](<#fd_shred_dest_delete>), so it acts as an internal implementation file for a shred destination service rather than a public executable.

The main logic computes destination seeds from shred data, slot, leader pubkey, and shred type, then uses ChaCha20-based random sampling and weighted sampling to choose destinations. [`fd_shred_dest_compute_first`](<#fd_shred_dest_compute_first>) handles the case where the source validator is the leader, and [`fd_shred_dest_compute_children`](<#fd_shred_dest_compute_children>) handles Turbine-style child selection for later hops. The file also contains helper logic for unstaked validator sampling and a public lookup helper, [`fd_shred_dest_pubkey_to_idx`](<#fd_shred_dest_pubkey_to_idx>), which maps a validator pubkey to its stored index.
